Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

give verb

also hand over, give as a present

classical

Catull. 61.124: dā nucēs puerīs
Hor. S. 1.1.25: puerīs … dant crūstula

dō, dare, dedī, datum

verb, first conjugation (short a: dare, datum)

The thing in the accusative and the person in the dative: dā mihi pilam. The a is short in every form except dās and dā.

Other words

  • dōnō, dōnāre, dōnāvī, dōnātum — give (as a present)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Catull. 1.1: cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum?; Mart. 6.30.2: sūme, tolle, dōnō

    alicui aliquid dōnāre, or aliquem aliquā rē dōnāre, to present someone with something.

  • trādō, trādere, trādidī, trāditum — hand over, hand (to someone)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Gell. 15.17.1: trāditās sibi tībiās

    Of passing something from one person’s hands to another’s.

Examples

  • dā nucēs puerīs

    give the children nutsCatull. 61.124

  • ut puerīs ōlim dant crūstula blandī doctōrēs, elementa velint ut discere prīma

    as coaxing teachers sometimes give children biscuits, so that they will want to learn their lettersHor. S. 1.1.25–26

  • cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum āridā modo pūmice expolītum?

    Whom shall I give this charming new little book to, just polished with dry pumice?Catull. 1.1–2

See also give back, give it here!, gift, receive, lend, offer.
